canonical.title: Naxos in 3–4 days: what to do, in what order, and what to skip

siblings.title: Chora on foot: Kastro, the Portara and the town core
siblings.summary: Chora's sights fit one long day on foot — Old Market early, Kastro mid-morning, Portara at sunset — and in 2026 the Archaeological Museum is in temporary quarters while the Mitropolis site museum is shut.

siblings.title: Naxos beaches, coast by coast: which beach for which day
siblings.summary: The west-coast strip south of Chora carries a 3–4 day trip; the east coast and the remote south are day-eaters you should skip unless a boat or a specific obsession justifies them.

siblings.title: The Naxos interior: mountain villages, marble country and Mt Zas
siblings.summary: Two driving loops and one dawn climb cover the whole interior: the Tragaea in a day, Zas plus Apeiranthos in a second, the emery north as an optional third.

siblings.title: Eating and drinking Naxian on a 3–4 day trip
siblings.summary: Naxos is the one Cycladic island that feeds itself — two PDO cheeses, a PGI potato, a PGI citron liqueur — and the eating is inland, not on the beach strip.

siblings.title: Naxos 2026: getting there, and whether you need a car
siblings.summary: Take the fast ferry from Piraeus, rent a car for 2 of your 3–4 days, and let the bus cover the beach days.

siblings.title: Naxos in 3–4 days: where to base yourself
siblings.summary: For a 3–4 night first visit, base in Chora (Naxos Town) — port, buses, dinner and a beach are all on foot.

siblings.title: Day trips off Naxos: which one earns a day of four
siblings.summary: On a 3–4 day first visit, no off-island ferry day trip beats Naxos itself; the only day-boat worth booking is a local Small Cyclades cruise.

sources.title: Naxos — Wikipedia
sources.claim: Naxos is 430 km² with a 1,003 m mountain in the middle; largest and most fertile Cycladic island; marble quarried before 550 BC.

sources.title: Naxos car & bus — Greeka
sources.claim: KTEL Line 1 runs the Agios Prokopios–Agia Anna–Plaka strip every 30 minutes in high season for €1.80–6.20; Line 3 to Pyrgaki only five times a day.

sources.title: Exploring Naxos by bus — Greek Island Buses
sources.claim: Apollonas is two buses a day (75 min); buy bus tickets before boarding, drivers sell none; the airport is 3 km out with no bus.

sources.title: Getting around Naxos — Cyclades.travel
sources.claim: Car hire runs roughly €50–70/day in July–August; taxi €3.50 base + ~€1/km; park only in Chora's municipal lots.

sources.title: Naxos buses — Greek Island Buses
sources.claim: All 14 KTEL bus routes radiate from Chora.

sources.title: Archaeological Collection of Gyroula (Sangri) — Ministry of Culture
sources.claim: Temple of Demeter at Gyroulas, Sangri: 08:30–15:30, closed Tuesdays, year-round, €5 including the site.

sources.title: Naxos climate — Climates to Travel
sources.claim: August averages ~27 °C with highs around 30 °C, 35–36 °C spells occur; the meltemi blows hardest July–August and strengthens through the afternoon.

sources.title: Greece heatwave 2026 — Wego
sources.claim: During the 21–23 July 2026 heatwave the Ministry of Culture shut the Acropolis from noon to 17:00.

sources.title: Sunrise and sunset in Naxos — General Blue
sources.claim: August 2026 sunset: 14 Aug 20:12, 20 Aug 20:04, 31 Aug 19:49.

sources.title: Archaeological Collection of Apeiranthos — Ministry of Culture
sources.claim: Apeiranthos Archaeological Collection: 08:30–15:30, closed Tuesday, year-round, €5; Early Bronze Age marble figurines and the Aroni plaques.

sources.title: Bazeos Tower
sources.claim: 2026 hours Tue–Fri 11:00–18:00, Sat–Sun 10:00–20:00, closed Monday.

sources.title: Naxos restaurants — Greeka
sources.claim: Axiotissa at Kastraki wants a reservation 3–4 days ahead in high season; Stou Lefteri in Apeiranthos has a flower-bedecked veranda.

sources.title: Vallindras distillery, Halki — Greek Gastronomy Guide
sources.claim: The Vallindras kitron distillery is on Halki's main square; kitron is one of only three Greek spirits with PDO status.

sources.title: Small Cyclades Lines — Express Skopelitis route
sources.claim: The Express Skopelitis leaves Naxos at 14:00–14:30 and returns 12:05–13:05 the next day.

sources.title: Meltemi wind and Greek ferries — Teleporio
sources.claim: Mid-July to August the meltemi hits 7–8 Beaufort and high-speed catamarans cancel first, at short notice.

sources.title: Panermos beach — Greeka
sources.claim: Panermos is 54 km from Chora with a single cafeteria and no public transport.

sources.title: Archaeological Museum of Naxos — Ministry of Culture
sources.claim: The Archaeological Museum is closed for renovation; a free temporary exhibition runs in the Ursulines building, 09:00–14:00, closed Tuesday.

sources.title: Naxos–Paros ferries — Ferryhopper
sources.claim: Paros is 30 minutes away with 10+ crossings a day, from €5.70.

sources.title: The Temple of Apollo (Portara) — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: Four marble blocks of roughly 20 tons each, all that was built of a temple of Apollo begun around 530 BC by Lygdamis; Palatia is joined to town by a paved footpath.

sources.title: Portara — Explore Naxos & Paros
sources.claim: Ten minutes from the harbour front: five across the causeway, five up the hill; very crowded at sunset, and the causeway turns slippery when the sea is choppy.

sources.title: Kastro of Chora — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: Three gates originally; two survive — Trani Porta (north-west) and Paraporti (south).

sources.title: Kastro of Chora — Greeka
sources.claim: Marco Sanudo founded the Kastro in 1207 as the seat of his Duchy of the Archipelago; the Glezos (Crispi) Tower is the only survivor of twelve; entry is free.

sources.title: Venetian Museum (Della Rocca-Barozzi) — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: Daily 10:00–15:00 and 19:00–22:00; staff-led walk-through of furniture, clothing and heirlooms.

sources.title: Naxos music festival — Rough Guides
sources.claim: The Domus Festival runs in the Venetian Museum's courtyard April to October; book in advance, ticket includes a glass of local wine or kitron.

sources.title: Agios Georgios beach — Naxaki
sources.claim: Agios Georgios is 1 km from the port, a flat 15-minute walk, Blue Flag, shallow and calm; free sand, paid sunbeds.

sources.title: Naxos Town (Chora) — Explore Naxos & Paros
sources.claim: Chora's old-town streets are too narrow to drive and parking is nonexistent; it is 25–30 minutes on foot from Agios Georgios to the Portara.

sources.title: Naxos Chora guide — The Common Wanderer
sources.claim: Old Market lanes are calmest before 09:00; Doukato fills up every night.

sources.title: Archaeological site of Grotta — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: Grotta is part of the Mycenaean-era capital, ~1300 BC, with some structures now submerged; viewed from above in fifteen minutes.

sources.title: Mitropolis Site Museum — Ministry of Culture
sources.claim: The ministry listing carries the notice that the museum will be closed from 01.08.2025.

sources.title: The real map of Naxos — Coralli
sources.claim: Driving times from Chora: Halki 25–30 min, Filoti 30–35 min, Apeiranthos 45–50 min, Apollonas 1 h 15.

sources.title: Mount Zas hike — The Common Wanderer
sources.claim: Agia Marina route: ~6 km return, ~450 m gain, 3–4 h, red paint and cairns, no water on route, 2 L per person minimum.

sources.title: Mount Zas and its cave — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: Mt Zas is the highest peak in the Cyclades at 1,003 m; the Zas Cave sits at 630 m with chambers up to 11 m.

sources.title: Zas Mountain — Tripadvisor
sources.claim: Reviewers report the heat already building by 08:30 and roughly an hour to the summit from the chapel; parking at Agia Marina is a small roadside lot.

sources.title: Mt Zas hiking trail 2 — Naxos Trek
sources.claim: The full Filoti circuit is 12.8 km, 5 h 20, challenging, with almost no shade.

sources.title: Naxos hiking trail 4 — Naxos Trek
sources.claim: Trail 4 from Halki: 7.2 km, 2 h 10, moderate, covering five churches from the 6th to 14th centuries.

sources.title: Halki, Naxos — Take Me To Greece
sources.claim: Halki is 16 km / 30 min from Chora at 280 m; Panagia Protothroni open Apr–Oct 08:00–20:00 free; Agios Georgios Diasoritis only 1 Jul–31 Aug, 11:00–13:30; free parking throughout.

sources.title: Panagia Drosiani — Elaiolithos
sources.claim: Panagia Drosiani was built in phases between the 4th and 6th centuries and is regarded as the oldest Byzantine church in the Cyclades, with 5th-century frescoes.

sources.title: Naxos's Byzantine legacy — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: Over 200 Byzantine churches on Naxos, more than 120 keeping original frescoes; most are locked and need the village caretaker.

sources.title: Temple of Sangri — Wikipedia
sources.claim: Built c. 530 BC in Naxian marble, an almost square 13.29 × 12.73 m, one of the earliest Ionic temples anywhere; partially re-erected in 1994.

sources.title: Apeiranthos — Wikipedia
sources.claim: Apeiranthos is 28 km from Chora at 650–700 m, population 773, Cretan-descended dialect, four museums.

sources.title: Geological Museum of Apeiranthos — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: Geological Museum, Apeiranthos: May–Sep 11:00–16:00, free.

sources.title: Driving in Naxos — Explore Naxos & Paros
sources.claim: Rental contracts routinely exclude damage on unpaved surfaces; don't drive the mountains after dark; the Apeiranthos→Moutsouna descent is one of the steepest roads in Greece.

sources.title: Naxos KTEL buses
sources.claim: 2026 inland one-way fares from Chora: Halki €2.30 / 30 min, Filoti €2.60 / 35 min, Apeiranthos €3.50 / 1 h.

sources.title: Naxos Festival 2026
sources.claim: The Naxos Festival runs at Bazeos Tower: collective exhibition 31 May – 11 Oct 2026, concerts through August.

sources.title: Bazeos Tower — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: The tower stands at the 12th km of the Chora–Agiassos road, built around 1600 as the monastery of Timios Stavros, restored and reopened in 2001.

sources.title: Kouroi of Melanes — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: The Flerio kouroi are open 24 h and free, with a designated car park and signposted footpaths.

sources.title: Kouroi of Flerio — Wikipedia
sources.claim: The garden kouros is 4.7 m long and 5–7 tonnes; the quarry kouros lies halfway up a 300 m marble outcrop.

sources.title: Apollonas kouros — Take Me To Greece
sources.claim: The Apollonas kouros is a 2.5-hour round trip for a 10-minute stop; free, 24 h, roadside parking.

sources.title: Cheimarros Tower — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: Cheimarros Tower is 14 km south of Filoti on the Kalantos road, a dead-end drive; unfenced and unstaffed.

sources.title: Emery transportation cable railway — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: The 1926–29 aerial ropeway ran 8,720 m from Stavrolagada to Moutsouna on 72 pylons and moved ~340,000 tonnes between 1929 and 1982; still standing, free.

sources.title: Koronos village — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: Koronos is 28 km from Chora at 540 m, seven neighbourhoods of whitewashed steps around the Platsa square; three car parks.

sources.title: Filoti village — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: Filoti is the largest village on the island, 18 km from Chora, ~1,800 residents; the three-day Panagia Filotitissa panigyri around 15 August is the biggest festival in the interior.

sources.title: How to read the Naxos coastline — Lagos Mare
sources.claim: The west coast is sheltered from the Etesian winds; the south coast takes their full force, and at Mikri Vigla by 2pm the water is choppy and the sand is blowing.

sources.title: Agios Prokopios guide — The Common Wanderer
sources.claim: Line 1 reaches Agios Prokopios in ~15 minutes for €1.80–2.10; it is a 20–30 minute walk between Agios Prokopios and Agia Anna or Plaka; the north-western public stretch is the sheltered one.

sources.title: Plaka beach — Greeka
sources.claim: Plaka is 4 km of white sand and dunes, part-organised at the north end, wild to the south.

sources.title: Alyko beach — Explore Naxos & Paros
sources.claim: Alyko is 18 km from Chora on a paved road, with zero sunbeds and one food truck; Hawaii Beach is a 5–10 minute walk from the main cove.

sources.title: Alyko hotel ruins — Atlas Obscura
sources.claim: The unfinished 1960s hotel at Alyko is now a set of concrete shells covered in murals.

sources.title: Mikri Vigla — Kite and Surf Naxos
sources.claim: The Mikri Vigla headland splits the bay: Parthena north is the sports beach, wind side-onshore; Limanaki south is the swimming one.

sources.title: Mikri Vigla Limanaki — Naxos Hotels
sources.claim: Limanaki/Sahara is wide golden sand running ~2 km toward Kastraki, protected from the north winds by the headland.

sources.title: Best beaches in Naxos — Santorini Dave
sources.claim: Kastraki takes the sunset behind Paros; Pyrgaki is three small sandy coves with a couple of tavernas; Agios Georgios has the best shallow water for toddlers.

sources.title: Axiotissa
sources.claim: Kastraki taverna sourcing from its own farm and named local producers; booking via the site's i-host link.

sources.title: Naxos best restaurants 2026 — travel.gr
sources.claim: Stou Lefteri in Apeiranthos does stuffed beef patty with Naxian graviera and handmade galaktoboureko; Amorginos does rosto and kalogero.

sources.title: The true taste of Naxos — travel.gr
sources.claim: Amorginos' grilled lamb chops with zamponi, graviera and anthotyro is the single best plate for tasting the products side by side; Axiotissa is run by Yiannis Vasilas and Sofia Dimakopoulou.

sources.title: Best restaurants in Naxos — Explore Naxos & Paros
sources.claim: To Spitiko Galaktoboureko in Halki is cash only and sells out — go early; most Naxos restaurants take no reservations at all.

sources.title: Fish & Olive, Halki
sources.claim: Katharina Bolesch and Alexander Reichardt's ceramics and jewellery gallery on Halki's square; 2026 season exhibition Cycladic Whispers, 10 May to mid-October.

sources.title: Arseniko Naxou PDO — protected food names register
sources.claim: Arseniko Naxou was EU-registered as a PDO on 20 January 2020.

sources.title: Cheeses of Naxos — Greek Gastronomy Guide
sources.claim: Graviera Naxou is the only Greek graviera made principally from cow's milk; arseniko is aged at least three months from non-pasteurised goat and sheep milk.

sources.title: EAS Naxos (Union of Agricultural Cooperatives)
sources.claim: Shop on the Chora seafront Mon–Sat 08:00–21:00, Sun 08:00–14:30; no public factory tour is advertised.

sources.title: Panigiria of Naxos — Music of Our Desire
sources.claim: For 15 August in Filoti: arrive after 23:00, the core runs midnight to 04:00, sleep in Chora; lamb on the spit, fava, local cheeses and carafe wine for a €5–10 collection.

sources.title: Day cruise to Rina and Schinoussa — Zas Tours
sources.claim: Local day cruise from Agia Anna 09:30→17:30, Rina cave plus Schinoussa/Iraklia, from €93.60; stops swapped by sea state.

sources.title: Piraeus–Naxos ferries — Ferryhopper
sources.claim: High-speed Piraeus–Naxos is 3h15–3h25 against 5h05 on Blue Star; the port is in Chora itself and walkable to town.

sources.title: Greek ferries — Santorini Dave
sources.claim: Book July–August crossings 2–3 months ahead; Blue Star is the weather-robust choice because catamarans cancel first in wind.

sources.title: Where to stay in Naxos — Santorini Dave
sources.claim: Chora suits couples and first-timers and is car-free viable; Halki/Filoti is 30–45 minutes from any beach, both ways, daily.

sources.title: Best Naxos hotels — The Common Wanderer
sources.claim: Chora is the cheapest area on the island and Agios Georgios beach is a ~5-minute walk; at Plaka the bus timetable will dictate your day.

sources.title: Naxos bus timetable — Naxos Insider
sources.claim: Line 1 runs roughly every 30 minutes in summer; Line 3 is unreliable for Alyko and Pyrgaki.

sources.title: A tour of the Kastro — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: The municipality's Kastro walk: in via Trani Porta → Della Rocca Barozzi tower → Tower of Crispi → Catholic Cathedral → Panagia Theoskepasti → Capuchin monastery → Archaeological Museum → Capella Kazatza → Ursuline school.

sources.title: Naxos Town (Bourgos) — Greeka
sources.claim: Bourgos is the Greek quarter spreading around and below the castle walls; the port strip holds the bus station, banks and car-rental desks.

sources.title: Vallindras distillery — Municipality of Naxos
sources.claim: The workshop dates to 1862, the citron liqueur to 1896, first exported 1928, fifth generation still running it.

sources.title: Vallindras Kitron Distillery — Tripadvisor
sources.claim: Reviewers consistently say the museum room is small with minimal signage — budget 10 minutes, not an hour.

sources.title: Hiking Mount Zas — Earth Trekkers
sources.claim: The last stretch to the Aria Spring trailhead is narrow with no guardrails and almost nowhere to turn around; the left turn past the cave is easy to miss.

sources.title: Knossos closed at heatwave peak — Keep Talking Greece
sources.claim: On 22 July 2026 Knossos was suspended 13:00–17:00 with 43 °C measured on site after two visitors fainted the day before.

sources.title: Moutsouna beach — Naxos.net
sources.claim: Moutsouna is 36.6 km from Chora on a road that is narrow and winding after Apeiranthos, with tavernas on the sand but no sunbed rental.
